adjudications.support: על אף האמור בסעיף 36א לחוק–יסוד: הכנסת, היום הקובע לגבי חוק התקציב לשנת 2013 יהיה יום כ"ד באב התשע"ג (31 ביולי 2013)
adjudications.reason: The text governs when the government must bring its budget and when budget failure dissolves the Knesset, so it engages separation of powers, and None is unavailable on the seq 19 and 31 reading that None means no value engaged. New s. 4(b) sets s. 36A aside for 2013 and fixes the determining day at 31 July, seven months into the fiscal year, lengthening the time the government may run on a continuing budget without a budget law; the seq 35 ruling treated spending without a budget law as a contradiction of the value and named the one-twelfth cap and the three-month clock as what kept it limited, and this text loosens the clock. It is limited because it covers one year and a date the Knesset itself fixed, and s. 4(a), which lets the Finance Committee set the tabling date, is an entrenching element the precedence rule subordinates. I adopt Coder B's reading, consistent with seqs 101, 105 and 109, which loosen the cap rather than the clock.

adjudications.support: Vote 38672: 62 for (Likud 29, Kulanu 10, Shas 7, UTJ 6, Yisrael Beiteinu 5, Jewish Home 4, faction 'חה"כ אורלי לוי-אבקסיס' 1), 38 against.
adjudications.reason: A named record of the final reading exists: the Knesset's plenum-vote table holds a roll call for the third reading (vote 38672), matching the press tally of 62-38, whereas vote 28637, which both coders used, is the second reading. At the third reading Mickey Rosenthal (Zionist Union) voted against, so Coder A's ground fails. But MK Orly Levy-Abekasis voted for, and the Knesset's records list her from 15.3.2017 to 30.4.2019 as member and chair of a separate one-member faction (ID 913), not among the six coalition factions both coders list; reading 'opposition faction' as any faction outside the coalition, a member of an opposition faction voted for. The value is No, on this record rather than Coder A's, and Coder B's blank rested on a record that is in fact available.

adjudications.support: לשם מימון ההוצאות הדרושות להתמודדות עם המשבר שנוצר בשל התפשטות נגיף הקורונה, ולמטרה זו בלבד
adjudications.reason: I read 'a specific interest of the sitting government' as an interest the government holds for itself (its tenure, composition, or the position of its members), not the public end for which it exercises a power conferred on it; otherwise every appropriation would be Yes. The text authorises 'the government', whichever holds office from April to December 2020, to spend set sums for the coronavirus crisis 'and for this purpose only', and names no officeholder; on the coders' own account the scheme was later amended under a different government (seqs 105 and 109). The explanatory notes (government bill of 6.4.2020) are unreachable: no archive capture, and the Knesset site is geo-blocked. I adopt Coder B's reading, and the same reading governs seqs 105, 109 and 118.

adjudications.support: על אף האמור בסעיף קטן (א), בחודשים אפריל עד דצמבר של שנת 2020 ... רשאית הממשלה להוציא את ההוצאות המפורטות להלן
adjudications.reason: The text engages separation of powers (the Knesset's control of public money), so None is unavailable (seq 19). For 2020 it lets the government spend without an approved budget law well beyond the s. 3B one-twelfth rule: monthly crisis shares, principal repayment up to NIS 100 billion and NIS 16.1 billion to National Insurance, with the detailed plan approved by the government and only laid before the Knesset; the seq 35 ruling treated spending without a budget law as a contradiction of the value, and this widens it. It is limited by its one-year term, Knesset-fixed sums and plan components, stated purpose, Finance Committee approval for changes above 15 percent, monthly reports and the permanent transparency duty in new s. 3B(b1), which are entrenching elements the precedence rule subordinates. I adopt Coder B's reading.

The amounts measure that authority, so the text is not value-neutral, and Coder A's None fails. Lowering to 10 percent the change threshold that needs Finance Committee approval is an entrenching element the precedence rule subordinates. Limited on the same bounds as seq 101; I adopt Coder B's value, now on the verbatim text Coder B lacked.

interpretive_rulings.reading_adopted: Item 4 is met only by a single-instance or sunset clause that by its own terms is confined to the sitting government's own measure (an act or decision of the government) or to the government's own term of office; a clause keyed to a Knesset's term or to a class of Knesset members does not qualify, even if on the day of passage it bears on the sitting government's appointments.
interpretive_rulings.reason: Section 6 is single-instance, but its object is members of the Twelfth Knesset who left their factions and agreements made with them, and its period is the Knesset's, not the government's. Whether it touches any ministerial or deputy-ministerial appointment depends on who held such posts, a fact outside the clause that the reader did not establish, and it would operate alike under any government formed during the Twelfth Knesset. If any clause operating during the government's tenure qualified, item 4's words 'own measure or term' would do no work. With no item 1 to 3 fact established, the cell is No, as the reader's own flag anticipates.

interpretive_rulings.reading_adopted: On the same reading as Q1, a sunset expressed as the term of a Knesset is not a sunset on the sitting government's own term under item 4.
interpretive_rulings.reason: Section 6 ends the arrangement with the term of the 20th Knesset, which would cover any government formed during that Knesset alike, and which does not track the government's term, since a government holds office until a new one is formed. The provisions it limits (ss. 23, 42C and 43 of Basic Law: The Knesset; ss. 26(5), 30A and 30B of Basic Law: The Government) apply to every minister and deputy minister alike, which the definition says satisfies no item. Section 5 does not change this: on the gazette text (ס"ח 2500, p. 248) it only exempts deputy ministers appointed before commencement from the new declaration of allegiance in s. 25(a1), unless they leave the Knesset, a transitional rule for all such incumbents alike rather than a clause on a measure of the government. No item 1 to 3 fact was found, so the cell is No.

interpretive_rulings.reading_adopted: Item 2 covers a formal step of the same kind as its examples, an act by an organ with authority to fix the legal position of, or open proceedings against, the person or the government's measure, and not a letter from the Knesset's legal adviser recording the government's non-compliance.
interpretive_rulings.reason: Each listed example either fixes the government's own legal position (the attorney general's opinion) or opens a proceeding (indictment, petition served). The Knesset legal adviser's letter of 26.11.2023 advises the Knesset's organs, binds the government to nothing and opens no proceeding, and its subject is the government's failure to file a report, not a measure of the government. The general-form sentence does not save the coding either: new s. 3A1(a1) is a permanent power that successor governments share, and on the day of passage it had no direct legal effect on the missed deadlines, since a deferral needed a later government proposal and Knesset approval. No.

deviations: No scratch subfolder was created and no file was written, because the caller's instruction forbade writing files; retrieved texts were streamed to standard output only. The harness itself saved two oversized command outputs (a bills-table listing and a plenum-vote table extract) to its tool-results folder.

Records beyond those the coders cite: the Knesset's plenum-vote and per-member result tables, faction and position tables, bill-status, plenum-session and bill-document tables, all from the Open Knesset mirror (production.oknesset.org/pipelines/data/); these are Knesset voting data and records, and they settle seqs 97 and 112 (coalition_only) and 118 (expedited).

Consolidated Basic Law texts on he.wikisource.org were read for context: Basic Law: The State Economy s. 3(b)(3) (seq 94) and the current Basic Law: The Knesset s. 36A (seq 80). The current s. 36A post-dates 2013, so it was not relied on for the 2013 default date; seq 80 rests on its own text and both coders' agreed reading of it as a one-year deferral.

Press read: the Walla report of 27.7.2021 and one search summary on the seq 112 tally; both were superseded by the named roll call. Search result lists showed titles of some court-related pages (a Globes article and an Adalah filing); none was opened.
For Part 2 Q2 the published gazette text of seq 89 (ס"ח 2500, 6.8.2015, via web.archive.org capture of fs.knesset.gov.il/20/law/20_lsr_313649.pdf) was read to check ss. 5 and 6.

seq 97 coalition_only: No is adopted on a different ground from Coder A's: Rosenthal voted against at the third reading; Levy-Abekasis's vote for decides it. That rests on reading a one-member faction recorded by the Knesset, outside the coalition, as an opposition faction; if 'opposition faction' were confined to factions elected as lists, the value would be Yes.

No departure from the batch 1 rulings: seqs 80, 101, 105 and 109 apply the seq 35 reading that spending without a budget law, bounded by the one-twelfth cap and the three-month clock, contradicts separation of powers to a limited extent; seq 94 applies the seq 19 and 31 readings.
Explanatory notes for seqs 80, 97, 101, 105 and 109 were unreachable (no archive capture; the Knesset site is geo-blocked).
